name: Photorealistic
means: A photograph rather than a drawing - continuous tone with no keyline anywhere, skin carrying pore texture and blood colour under it, and real lens behaviour: a focal plane that actually falls off, corner falloff, catchlights.
prose: a photograph, natural skin with visible pore texture and fine stray hair, catchlights in the eyes, 50mm lens at f/2.0, shallow focal plane falling off behind the subject, soft directional daylight, continuous tone with no outlines
negative_add: anime, cel shading, flat colour, thick outlines, illustration, painting, 3d render, cgi, plastic skin, airbrushed
works_for: stills reliably. Video - MEASURED, and the result is the opposite of the old prediction. Faces and hands did NOT boil: skin texture and facial structure hold cleanly through ~5.7s. What fails is the SHOT - at 8.04s the subject walked out of frame entirely and the clip ends on an empty street (detail octiles 1.00 ... 0.89 0.52, a cliff in the final eighth). At 4s the same clip is clean (detail 0.964). Keep photographic shots to about 4 seconds; the ceiling here is composition stability, not texture. Also note the untested CAPABILITIES.md claim that Wan is the more faithful i2v remains unmeasured.
note: Do not run this on the anime checkpoint. `photorealistic` is a STANDING NEGATIVE in this project - studio/tags/photorealistic.json records that in the positive on Animagine it returns waxy semi-real faces and lost line, the worst of both worlds. It needs qwen. On qwen the negative above is close to inert at cfg 1.0 with the Lightning LoRA; if a render drifts illustrative, drop the LoRA and run 20 steps at cfg 2.5-4.0 so the negative actually bites. This is a STYLE, not a look: it changes what the model draws. What colour the result ends up is still the grade's job. | Downgraded to untested: NOTHING in this library was rendered when it was authored, so every strength and engine call is a considered prediction. This project's own standard - written on the Illustrious checkpoint card - is that a recommendation is not a measurement.
verdict: Skin texture and real lens falloff. Sits close to the control at 21.0 because qwen's baseline IS photographic - that is agreement, not failure.
verified_by: Looked at, against the no-style control at the same seed with the same subject. studio/_tools/style_examples.py

video_verdict.failure: THE SHOT fails, not the style - the subject walks out of frame by 8s
video_verdict.saw: The most important clip in the sweep, and its failure has nothing to do with style. Skin texture, pores and facial structure hold beautifully through frame 137 - the predicted melting of faces and hands simply does not occur. Then the subject WALKS OUT OF FRAME. By frame 192 she is an out-of-focus red blur exiting stage left and the shot is an empty street. The octiles are flat and then cliff (1.00 1.01 1.01 0.97 0.97 0.94 0.89 0.52); detail is 0.510 at 8s but 0.964 at 4s. The 0.510 is measuring 'the subject left', not 'the texture dissolved'. At 4 seconds this clip is completely usable.
video_verdict.measured_on: One 193-frame (8.04s) LTX-2.3 image-to-video clip, workflow 12_ltx23_i2v_audio.json at its shipping settings, from a keyframe rendered on this style's own engine at 1280x704. Held constant across every style in the sweep: subject, keyframe seed 7204, video seed 8801, motion prompt, clip length. MEASURED BY RENDERING AND LOOKING, NOT PREDICTED.
video_verdict.caveats: boil is NOT a style-stability number in this sweep - it tracks how much the clip moved, and the identical motion prompt produced motion from 0.345 to 2.772 across styles. detail is the load-bearing number, and it too drops when the COMPOSITION changes rather than the texture. Read both against the strips. n=1 clip, one subject, one seed.
